stature.basis: Heritage of the settler and soldier families (British, Irish and German descent); varied so the seven differ. Height for age: the CDC 2000 stature-for-age table at the 5th centile for the age on 14 Aug 1812. Not a measurement. Why that centile: Steckel 1985 finds slave children below the first centile of modern standards and Komlos 2003 puts American apprentices of 14 at the 0.8th, while American adults reached about the 20th-30th; free children of a fed frontier household are set at the 5th, a soldier's or settler's family on rations.
